note: Single source of truth for this brain's data contract. Templates, JSON Schemas, the catalog, the portable bundle schema, the skill stubs, the directory indexes, the derived indexes and (in cut 2) the SQLite DDL are all GENERATED from this file. Never edit a generated artifact; edit this and run `brain generate`. READING ORDER -- the top-level keys are ordered as a narrative, separated by blank lines, rather than nested into groups: (1) what this contract is -- note, versions, provenance, governance, and the policies it is written under; (2) the vocabulary the schema is written in -- data types, actors, and the classification ladder, each defined before it is used; (3) the schema itself -- common_fields and types, which are 59% of the file; (4) the files it produces -- reserved, exempt, derived, and the portable bundle schema. Grouping these into nested objects was considered and rejected: the groups are wildly uneven, the boundaries are genuinely ambiguous (classification is both vocabulary and policy), and nesting would lengthen every access path and every provenance entry for no functional gain.

provenance.note: What comes from the OKF specification and what is ours. This block exists because the file used to be named okf.json, which implied the whole thing was the standard -- it is not, and the confusion had a cost: it was unclear what to update when a new OKF version ships. The answer is now exact: the items under `from_okf`, and nothing else.
provenance.ours: Everything not listed above. OKF leaves `type` producer-defined and takes no position on a field-level type system, data classification, stewardship, derived files, severity policy or generation -- which is most of this file by volume. Our additions extend the standard; they never contradict it, and the validator keeps the two levels apart so a bundle stays OKF-conformant even when it fails our profile.
provenance.completeness_rule: Every entry of `common_fields` must appear in exactly one of the three lists. A new common field therefore forces a conscious answer to 'is this the standard's or ours?', which is the question the old filename made impossible to answer. Enforced by kernel/tests/test_roundtrip.py.

governance.note: Makes this contract a governed artifact rather than a file someone edits. Governance that lives only in prose is what v1 had, and it enforced nothing.
governance.change_process: A contract change is a PR to the starter, never a local edit. Bump `profile_version` when tightening a constraint. No type enters without a competency question that needs it.
governance.enforcement: `brain.py validate` on pre-commit (only what changes) and in CI (the whole bundle). A control nobody runs is not a control.

language_policy.note: The rule, stated as a test rather than a preference: ANY string this contract renders into an artifact a person reads is content and is Spanish; everything else is configuration and is English. In practice that means `note` is always English -- it is commentary for whoever maintains the contract, and nothing renders it -- while `placeholder`, `guide`, `heading`, the `bundle_schema` strings, the `derived_files` strings and the classification `description`/`handling` are always Spanish. Field KEYS stay as production writes them. Enum VALUES split by scope: per-type enums are Spanish because they live in 10.000 documents and renaming them is a corpus migration; the two common-field enums (`status`, `classification`) are English because they travel in every document next to each other and `status` comes from OKF.
language_policy.history: Two leaks were found by applying this rule after the fact. The classification `description`/`handling` had been translated to English and were rendering inside the bundle's own ESQUEMA.md. And `placeholder` did not exist: the generator fell back to `note`, so `Sistema.dueño` emitted a full English paragraph about migration costs and check numbers into the user's document. Separating the two roles is what fixed it -- one string cannot serve both an engineer and a reader.

location_rules.note: Locations are ROUTING data, not documentation. `brain place` answers 'where does this document go', so /x-procesar-inbox no longer decides destinations from prose spread across three skill modules, and V19 validates against the same declaration. A pattern may be a plain string or an object with `when` (same shape as derived_files.where) and `role`.
location_rules.placeholders: Every `{name}` in a path must be a field the type declares. Enforced by kernel/tests/test_roundtrip.py -- making locations routable is what exposed that Insumo, Playbook and Iniciativa itself referenced `{proyecto}` without declaring it.
location_rules.ambiguity: If exactly one pattern applies, `brain place` answers. If several do, it returns the candidates and the agent chooses. The tool removes the prose, never the judgement.

roles.archive: dónde queda tras /x-cierre-periodo; válido para validar, nunca para enrutar

frontmatter_rules.note: Rules an agent must follow when WRITING frontmatter. They exist because our parser is deliberately lenient and the viewer the user opens is not: a value our validator accepted made Obsidian and VS Code fail with 'mapping values are not allowed here', and users reported it. Enforced by V18, so this is a check and not a suggestion.
agent_rules_es: Nunca escribas `: ` (dos puntos y espacio) dentro de un valor sin entrecomillar. Es el indicador de clave y valor en YAML, y rompe el visor. Usa una coma, un guion o un punto y coma — o entrecomilla el valor completo.

Nunca escribas ` #` (espacio y almohadilla) dentro de un valor: YAML lo lee como comentario y **borra en silencio todo lo que sigue**. Ni siquiera `--fix` puede recuperarlo, porque no hay forma de saber si querías un comentario.
No empieces un valor por `- ? : , [ ] { } # & * ! | > ' " % @` — todos son indicadores de YAML.
Para un campo de texto, si el valor es `true`, `no`, `on`, `null` o parece un número, entrecomíllalo: YAML lo convertiría de tipo.
Ante la duda, entrecomilla con comillas dobles y escapa las que haya dentro. Entrecomillar de más nunca rompe nada.
La prosa larga va en el cuerpo del documento, no en el frontmatter. El frontmatter es para metadatos cortos y consultables.
frontmatter_rules.auto_fix: `brain.py validate --fix` entrecomilla los valores cuyo significado no cambia al hacerlo, y lo verifica reparseando cada línea antes de escribirla. Los que sí cambiarían de significado se reportan para que los resuelva una persona.

severity_policy.note: Migration ladder. Constraints that v1's templates already guaranteed ship as `error`. Constraints introduced by OKF v0.2 ship as `warning` in profile_version 1, so a real brain does not light up on day one. Tightening a constraint means flipping it to `error` and bumping profile_version.

datetime.note: ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset, e.g. 2026-08-28T14:00:00Z

list.note: inline [a, b] or block; element type in `of`

link.note: bundle-relative path starting with /, or the reserved /raw/ pointer

typed-ref.note: link whose target must carry the type named in `to`

type-key.hint: el slug del proyecto; `transversal` si no pertenece a ninguno
type-key.note: reference by KEY VALUE rather than by path: the value must match the `key` field of some document of type `to`. Exists because `proyecto: 2026-q3-erp` is written that way in every document in production -- turning it into a link would be a corpus migration. `sentinels` lists values that are valid without resolving.

person-ref.note: accountability pointer. A bundle link to a Persona resolves and is checked; free text is tolerated and reported by V17 as unresolved stewardship. Migration-friendly by design: ownership becomes queryable progressively instead of behind a wall of errors.

actor.note: matches one of the patterns in `actors`

map.note: single-level inline mapping; member types in `fields`

actors.note: Per OKF v0.2 section 7. Trust classification keys off the `human:` prefix, so it must be used for hand-authored or human-confirmed content. There is no `agent:` prefix -- agents use producer/version.

classification.note: Proposed taxonomy: the organization had none defined. Four levels ordered from least to most restrictive. The ORDER is load-bearing -- V16 compares against each type's floor. If the organization adopts its own taxonomy, replace it here and every generated artifact follows.
classification.min_note: Per-type floor. `min_classification` is declared only where it exceeds `default_min`, so the exception is the thing you read. A document BELOW its floor is an ERROR, never a warning: it is the one classification control that does not relax during migration.
classification.value_language_note: These enum VALUES are English, unlike every other enum in this contract. The reason the others stayed Spanish was migration cost -- they live in the frontmatter of every document in production. This field is new in v2, so no document carries it and the cost is zero. It also sits next to `status` (draft|stable|deprecated, from OKF) in every single document, and two adjacent lifecycle enums in two languages is a wart. The resulting line is principled rather than arbitrary: COMMON fields follow OKF and are English; PER-TYPE fields follow production and are Spanish.

levels.description: Puede salir de la organización sin daño.
Uso interno; sin daño material si circula dentro de la organización.
levels.handling: No compartir fuera. Es el piso por defecto: la ausencia de clasificación nunca significa público.

levels.handling: No compartir fuera del equipo con necesidad de conocer. Revisar antes de exportar un cerebro que los contenga.

levels.description: Material regulatorio, legal o de seguridad. Su divulgación tiene consecuencias formales.
levels.handling: Requiere autorización explícita del dueño del dato. Revisar antes de cualquier compartición o respaldo fuera del perímetro.

type.note: The only field OKF always requires. A concept carrying just `type` is fully conformant.

description.placeholder: qué es y por qué importa, en una oración
description.note: one sentence: what it is and why it matters

tags.hint: etiquetas cortas para agrupar; lista vacía es válida

classification.note: Sensitivity level. The allowed values are RESOLVED from the taxonomy at load time rather than repeated here -- writing the list twice in one file is exactly the drift this contract exists to prevent, and it had been written twice. Required, but only a warning in profile 1 because the production corpus does not carry it yet. Each type declares a `min_classification`; going below it is an error, not a warning. Replaces v1's prose rule (`no sensitive data`), which enforced nothing because it lived inside a template guide string.

verified.note: OKF v0.2. A bare mapping MUST be treated as a one-element list. A document with no verified entry from a `human:` actor is a proposal, not knowledge -- this is the human-review rule expressed in the schema instead of in a prompt.

timestamp.note: v1 field, not part of OKF. `brain validate --fix` moves it to generated.at and leaves generated.by as a declared gap when git history cannot resolve it.

Glosario.description: A term, acronym or piece of internal jargon
Glosario.note: STRUCTURAL, decided 2026-08-31. No competency question needs it as a subject and it declares no required fields -- its content is prose by nature, so nothing about it is queryable. The cutting rule would drop it; it stays for the reason `Insumo` and `Indice` stay: it serves by being READ, not queried. Cutting it would also solve nothing -- OKF requires a `type` on every knowledge file, production holds 8 of these, and no other type houses the definition of a term. Not modelled in the cut-2 projection beyond its identity.

Playbook.description: A reusable step-by-step process, meant to be followed again
Playbook.note: Split from `Analisis` on 2026-08-31. It was defined as a reusable process OR an archived analysis -- the OR was the defect, and the competency questions forced the answer the cutting rule promised: CQ-44 asks for processes to reuse (decision: reutilizar en vez de improvisar) while CQ-34 asks for precedent not to repeat. Different `decision`, `frequency` and `answer_shape`, so two types. The cut: a Playbook is FOLLOWED, an Analisis is CONSULTED -- if a document does not say `next time, do this`, it is not a Playbook. MIGRATION: production holds 23 documents of this type needing triage by hand; /x-nueva-iniciativa creates analisis-inicial.md as a Playbook, and those are Analisis. STILL UNRESOLVED: v1 cerebro/GOALS.md carries this type and is neither -- it is period objectives, and no competency question asks for it.

Analisis.note: The half of the old `Playbook` that is consulted rather than followed, split out on 2026-08-31. Kept because CQ-34 -- what is on record about this from earlier periods -- is answered by archived analyses as much as by decisions and initiatives, and its decision is `no repetir un intento ya hecho`. Spanish and unaccented, like `Reunion` and `Decision`. Named deliberately away from `Informe`, `Entregable` and `Recurso`: the competency-question research flagged the emitted deliverable and `Recurso` as separate unnamed gaps, and taking those names now would claim ground that belongs to them.

Indice.description: A bundle-scope index, regenerated from frontmatter
Indice.note: The 12th type, and the one addition to v1's catalog of 11. It exists because OKF requires typed frontmatter on every non-reserved .md, and `index.md`/`log.md` are the only reserved names -- so a bundle-level derived index such as PREGUNTAS-ABIERTAS.md needs a type to be conformant. Never hand-written: `brain derive` and `brain generate` own it.

reserved_files.note: The filenames OKF reserves. `format` selects which structural check applies, so neither the name nor the rule is repeated in code.

index.md.note: directory index; no frontmatter except at the bundle root, which may carry okf_version only

log.md.note: date-grouped change history, newest first; headings are ISO YYYY-MM-DD

exempt_files.note: Exempt from the PROFILE checks only -- never from OKF conformance. OKF requires typed frontmatter on every non-reserved .md, so these still need a `type`; what they do not need is to match a catalog type's field set.
exempt_files.PERFIL.md: owner context in free prose; written by /x-setup

derived_files.note: Regenerated deterministically by `brain derive`. These grow with the brain; having the model rewrite them by hand is Slope A, the cost this contract exists to remove. Each entry declares what to select, how to filter, sort and render, so the engine knows nothing about this brain's types by name. Each also declares the `type` its generated frontmatter carries, so a derived file is fully OKF-conformant with nobody maintaining it.

bundle_schema.note: The single generated human-readable spec. A separate kernel-side CATALOGO.md existed and was deleted: it carried the same tables, and its only real advantage -- richer columns -- was an accident of improving one file and not the other. One derived spec, living where the documents are. Content of the portable ESQUEMA.md written into the bundle. It lives here rather than in code because it is content, not configuration: it is what someone who receives the `cerebro/` folder reads to understand it without the kernel. Spanish, like the rest of the bundle.
bundle_schema.title: Esquema de datos de este cerebro
bundle_schema.description: Cómo leer esta base de conocimiento: tipos, campos, convenciones y clasificación.
bundle_schema.intro: Este archivo hace al cerebro **autodescriptivo y portable**: cualquier persona o sistema que reciba la carpeta `cerebro/` puede entender su base de conocimiento leyendo esto, sin necesitar el kernel. Se genera desde el contrato; no se edita a mano.
conventions: **Bundle**: esta carpeta es la raíz. Los enlaces que empiezan con `/` se resuelven desde aquí.

**Puntero externo `/raw/...`**: apunta a las fuentes crudas del sistema que hospeda este cerebro, fuera del bundle. Si recibiste el cerebro sin sus fuentes, esos enlaces estarán rotos: es esperado, el conocimiento integrado está completo igual.
**Enlaces rotos**: se toleran. Representan conocimiento aún no escrito, no errores.
Todo `.md` de conocimiento lleva frontmatter con `type`. Se exceptúan `index.md` (índice por carpeta) y `log.md` (historia de cambios, más reciente primero).
Las fuentes de cada afirmación van al final de cada documento, bajo `# Citations`.

structure.01-proyectos/: Trabajo con fecha de fin: una carpeta por proyecto, con su CONTEXT.md, insumos, reuniones, decisiones y preguntas.
structure.02-areas/: Responsabilidades continuas. Incluye `personas/` con las fichas y el organigrama.
structure.03-recursos/: Referencia: sistemas y herramientas, glosario, y lo que el rol necesite.

bundle_schema.classification_intro: Cada documento lleva un nivel de clasificación. Cada tipo tiene un **mínimo**: por debajo de él, el documento es inválido. Revisa esto antes de compartir o exportar el cerebro.
bundle_schema.types_intro: Los campos de cada tipo, con su obligatoriedad y valores admitidos. Suficiente para leer los datos —o regenerar las plantillas— sin el kernel.
bundle_schema.type_labels_note: Bundle-facing one-liner per type. The `description` on each type is engineering metadata in English, for the catalog and the JSON Schemas; this is the same thing said to the person who receives the brain, in the language of the brain. The renderer falls back to `description` when a label is missing.

type_labels.Iniciativa: El CONTEXT.md de cada proyecto u objetivo con entidad propia.
type_labels.Insumo: Documento recibido, convertido a markdown, con puntero a su original en /raw/.
type_labels.Decision: Registro de una decisión: contexto, alternativas y consecuencias.
type_labels.Pregunta: Duda abierta, con estado y responsable.
type_labels.Persona: Ficha de una persona de la organización.
type_labels.Sistema: Ficha de un sistema, herramienta, producto o proceso.
type_labels.Lineamiento: Estándar, política o regla de trabajo vigente.
type_labels.Diagrama: Diagrama en Mermaid o PlantUML, con su contexto.
type_labels.Glosario: Término, sigla o jerga interna de la organización.
type_labels.Playbook: Proceso reutilizable paso a paso, para volver a seguirlo.
type_labels.Analisis: Estudio puntual de un asunto, archivado como precedente.
type_labels.Indice: Índice de alcance de bundle, regenerado desde el frontmatter.
